investigation.title: Remote Agent Creation Blocked by Swarm Agent Quota Exhaustion (HTTP 409)
investigation.summary: All three remote-agents eval checks (remote-agent-create, remote-agent-state, remote-agent-runtime) failed at 2026-06-17T04:01:54Z with an identical HTTP 409 response from POST /api/agents, carrying the swarm error "conflict: agent quota exceeded: limit is 100". Because the failure occurs at the agent creation step shared by all three checks, no evidence (orgId, agentId, vmIdPresent, remoteState) was ever collected, causing a complete contract gap for the remote-agent-create eval.
investigation.rootCause: The production swarm backend rejected POST /api/agents with HTTP 409 because the eval org has reached the hard agent quota limit of 100. The createAgent call in infra/evals/status/run-status-probes.mjs (line 1339) is the first operation in every remote-agents check; when it fails, all downstream evidence collection is skipped and all three sibling checks fail with the same message. This is an eval infrastructure failure caused by a resource-limit condition in the production swarm API, not a code defect in the eval runner itself. No user-traffic or incident signals are present in the supplied evidence, so impact is scoped to the observability eval suite.

investigations.title: Remote Agent Creation Blocked by Swarm Agent Quota Exhaustion (HTTP 409)
investigations.summary: All three remote-agents eval checks (remote-agent-create, remote-agent-state, remote-agent-runtime) failed at 2026-06-17T04:01:54Z with an identical HTTP 409 response from POST /api/agents, carrying the swarm error "conflict: agent quota exceeded: limit is 100". Because the failure occurs at the agent creation step shared by all three checks, no evidence (orgId, agentId, vmIdPresent, remoteState) was ever collected, causing a complete contract gap for the remote-agent-create eval.
investigations.rootCause: The production swarm backend rejected POST /api/agents with HTTP 409 because the eval org has reached the hard agent quota limit of 100. The createAgent call in infra/evals/status/run-status-probes.mjs (line 1339) is the first operation in every remote-agents check; when it fails, all downstream evidence collection is skipped and all three sibling checks fail with the same message. This is an eval infrastructure failure caused by a resource-limit condition in the production swarm API, not a code defect in the eval runner itself. No user-traffic or incident signals are present in the supplied evidence, so impact is scoped to the observability eval suite.

investigations.summary: All three observability evals for the remote-agents feature (remote-agent-create, remote-agent-state, remote-agent-runtime) failed at 2026-06-17T04:01:55–57Z with an identical HTTP 409 response from POST /api/agents: the swarm backend rejected agent creation because the org-scoped remote agent quota of 100 has been reached. Because agent creation is the first step in the eval probe (run-status-probes.mjs line 1372 calls createAgent), no agent was provisioned and therefore no runtime evidence (orgId, agentId, model, provider, message) was collected, causing the expected-output contract to fail completely.
investigations.rootCause: The production-api swarm backend is returning HTTP 409 with error code "conflict" and message "conflict: agent quota exceeded: limit is 100" for every POST /api/agents call made by the observability eval runner. The eval probe for remote-agent-runtime (and its siblings remote-agent-create and remote-agent-state) all call createAgent as their first substantive step; when that call is rejected, the probe cannot proceed, no evidence is captured, and the expected-output contract (requiring orgId, agentId, model, provider, message) is entirely unmet. This is a shared upstream dependency failure at the agent-creation layer, not an isolated failure of any single check's logic. No prior passing run is recorded, so the duration of the quota condition is unknown from this evidence alone.
proof: failed-check.message: POST /api/agents failed with 409 — error body contains 'conflict: agent quota exceeded: limit is 100', confirming the swarm backend rejected creation before any agent was provisioned.
sibling.remote-agent-create and sibling.remote-agent-state carry the identical 409 message (sameMessage: true), establishing that all three checks share the same failure point at POST /api/agents.

verifierContext.siblingCorrelation.likelySharedDependencyFailure: true — the verifier independently flagged a shared upstream dependency failure across production-api/remote-agent-create and production-api/remote-agent-state.

expected-output.missing-required-evidence: all five required evidence keys (orgId, agentId, model, provider, message) are absent, consistent with the probe aborting at createAgent before any downstream steps could run.
failed-check.evidence is an empty object {}, confirming zero evidence was collected during the run.

source-context.infra/evals/status/run-status-probes.mjs:1364-1372 shows the probe calls createAgent(args, track, 'remote', null, orgId) immediately after setup — a 409 at this call would prevent all subsequent evidence collection.
failed-check.timing: latencyMs=1158 — the check resolved in ~1 second, consistent with a fast rejection at the creation endpoint rather than a timeout or runtime hang.

source-context.infra/evals/status/check-expectations.json:194-198 confirms the contract requires orgId, agentId, model, provider, message and asserts message containsIgnoreCase 'hello from aura' — none of these could be satisfied without a successfully created agent.
possibleCauses: Primary — Org-level remote agent quota exhausted: the swarm backend enforces a hard limit of 100 remote agents per org. The eval runner's probe account or org has accumulated 100 or more live remote agents (possibly from prior eval runs that were not cleaned up), causing every new creation attempt to be rejected with HTTP 409.

Secondary — Eval cleanup (withCleanup / track) failed in a prior run, leaving orphaned remote agents that count against the quota. The runner uses withCleanup (run-status-probes.mjs line 1370) to deregister agents after each probe; if cleanup was interrupted or errored, agents may have accumulated over multiple runs.
Tertiary — The probe service account or org was recently migrated to a lower quota tier, reducing the effective limit below the number of agents already present.

Lower confidence — A swarm-side bug is incorrectly counting agents toward the quota (e.g., counting soft-deleted or terminated agents as active). This would require swarm-side investigation to confirm or rule out.

Add a quota headroom check as a prerequisite gate that runs before remote-agent-create, remote-agent-state, and remote-agent-runtime, so quota exhaustion is surfaced as its own named failure rather than a confusing 409 on the creation step.
Consider a dedicated eval for the swarm agent quota API endpoint to track quota usage trends over time and alert when approaching the limit.

investigations.title: Image Generation Stream Eval Failure: SESSION_OPEN_FAILED (404) on /api/generate/image/stream in production-api
investigations.summary: The image-generation-stream eval for the production-api runtime environment failed immediately (latencyMs=2034) because the agent runtime returned a SESSION_OPEN_FAILED error with a 404 on the /api/generate/image/stream endpoint, preventing the stream from ever reaching a generation_completed frame or producing an image URL. Both required contract assertions — frameTypes contains "generation_completed" and imageUrlPresent equals true — were violated as a direct consequence of this session-open failure.
investigations.rootCause: The agent runtime harness backing the /api/generate/image/stream endpoint in the production-api environment was unreachable or returned a 404 at session-open time, causing the SSE stream to emit a generation_error frame with code SESSION_OPEN_FAILED instead of progressing to generation_completed. This is an eval-infrastructure or runtime-harness availability failure localized to the production-api runtime environment and the image generation session-open path; no user-traffic or incident signals are present in the supplied evidence, so this cannot be characterized as a user-facing outage.
proof: failed-check.evidence: frameTypes observed = ["generation_start", "generation_error", "message"]; generation_completed is absent; imageUrlPresent = false.

failed-check.evidence: generation_error frame carries code=SESSION_OPEN_FAILED and message="agent runtime endpoint not found (404): the harness is unreachable or running an incompatible version. Verify the harness deployment and the LOCAL_HARNESS_URL / SWARM_BASE_URL configuration."
failed-check.timing: latencyMs=2034, well under the warningLatencyMs=180000 threshold, confirming the stream failed at session-open rather than timing out during generation.

expected-output.contract: assertions require frameTypes contains "generation_completed" (infra/evals/status/check-expectations.json line 271) and imageUrlPresent equals true (line 272); both are violated.

source-context.infra/evals/status/run-status-probes.mjs:1431-1440: runner calls apiSse(args, "/api/generate/image/stream", ...) — the 404 is returned from this endpoint before any generation frame is emitted.

source-context.infra/evals/status/features.json:237-245: the production-api variant of image-generation-stream is registered as required=false with statusImpact=informational, confirming this check does not gate a required status signal.
failed-check.message: composite failure message confirms both the 404 harness error and the two assertion failures as a single causal chain.
possibleCauses: The agent runtime harness is not deployed or not reachable at the URL configured by LOCAL_HARNESS_URL or SWARM_BASE_URL in the production-api eval environment, causing the /api/generate/image/stream session-open request to return 404.

The harness is deployed but is running an incompatible version that no longer exposes the /api/generate/image/stream route or has changed the session-open protocol, resulting in a 404 on that specific path.

The SWARM_BASE_URL or LOCAL_HARNESS_URL environment variable is misconfigured, empty, or pointing to a stale/wrong host for the production-api runtime environment, so the request is routed to a server that does not handle this endpoint.
A transient deployment gap (e.g., harness pod restart, rolling update, or scale-to-zero) caused the endpoint to be temporarily unavailable at the moment the eval ran at 2026-06-17T04:01:57Z.
